name: Showering guide

lead: A showering guide sets out when and how to wash so that skin looks clear, hair is clean and body odor does not undercut a person's appearance. It is the basic hygiene layer beneath other looksmaxxing work.

Forum guides give specific routines; dermatology bodies give general advice on temperature, duration and moisturizing. Research directly on 'looksmaxxing showers' is absent, though studies of mild cleansers and skin barrier care exist.

paras: A popular looksmax.org guide recommends a scrubbing glove, shower gel, a bar soap and deodorant, and showering on waking and before bed, plus after sweating. The American Academy of Dermatology's general guidance for dry skin is brief showers in warm water, limited cleanser, patting dry and moisturizing right after.
Frequent hot showers with strong cleansers can dry the skin, which dermatology bodies note especially for people with dry skin or eczema. Shower habits are otherwise low-risk.

chain: Cleaner skin and hair, less body odor
angle.text: Regular washing keeps skin and hair clean and limits odor, which supports every other grooming step. Moisturizing after the shower is the part dermatology guidance ties most directly to skin condition.

lead: A showering guide is a looksmaxxing description of how often to wash and what to use so that skin, hair and body odor are in good order. Cleanliness is treated as the baseline of grooming: clear skin, fresh-smelling and tidy presentation are visible and noticeable to others before any structural change.[1]

In 2025 a looksmax.org member posted a widely replied-to guide that begins with the line that some people still shower poorly, and lists a scrubbing glove, shower gel, a natural soap bar and a roll-on deodorant as the items needed.[1] It recommends showering once on waking and once before bed, and again after a workout or anything sweaty.[1]

Dermatology guidance is more conservative about frequency and heat: the American Academy of Dermatology advises showers of five to ten minutes in warm rather than hot water, with a gentle cleanser applied where needed and moisturizer applied right after drying.[2] Showers themselves are a recent norm; home showers became common in many places only in the 1970s.[3]

paras: The guide format is common on looksmaxxing forums: a numbered routine covering water temperature, order of washing, cleansers and drying. The 2025 looksmax.org post states that its text was formatted with an AI tool from the author's notes and gives a short summary, 'shower at least twice daily', adding more after sweating or getting dirty.[1]

The AAD's advice for dry skin is to use warm, not hot, water, keep showers to five to ten minutes, use a gentle cleanser only where needed such as armpits and groin, pat skin dry, and apply a fragrance-free moisturizer while skin is still damp.[2]
A review of mild cleansing in atopic dermatitis describes synthetic-detergent (syndet) bars as milder than traditional soap and used with proper washing as part of eczema management.[4]

Waterfalls were early natural showers, Greeks and Romans had communal shower rooms, and a hand-pumped shower was patented in England in 1767. Indoor plumbing made them practical in the 19th century, and home showers became common in the 1970s.[3]

No studies found on looksmaxxing shower routines. Related research includes a review of syndet cleansing bars in atopic dermatitis.[4] A small pilot study examined shower steps and time in people with brain injury, which concerns daily-living function rather than appearance.[5]

lore.intro: Showering guides are posted on looksmax.org as basic hygiene advice, with replies mixing agreement and jokes.[1]
